corrections.reason: AC-022 keeps the rule and points to the confirmation; new AC-033 (native confirmation on reload or close), AC-034 (application dialog when leaving to the root or another country) and AC-035 (going back does not ask); REQ-005, AC-008, AC-027, AC-028 and AC-030 extended. Details the owner did not state are raised as open questions N1 to N5.

AC-001 makes the root heading and page title front-end fallback copy in Spanish; AC-015 adds a visible loader with an announced Spanish fallback label and a reduced-motion variant; AC-008 and REQ-004 list the fallback copy.

The proposal records the answers to Q1, Q2, Q3, Q5, Q7, Q8 and Q9 as owner answers accepting the proposed resolutions (Q1: format only, no check-character validation); no earlier question remains open.

derived.reason: The story opens the application 'in the context of a country' without saying how the country is chosen; ADR-001 and the architecture place the choice at the root address and the country in the first route segment. The owner answered that the root page copy is front-end fallback copy (rejection R-2).

ADR-001 lists an unknown or unpublished country code in the address as a risk whose behavior the specs must define; the story does not define it. The owner accepted exact matching with a fallback message (rejection R-3, Q5).

The design reference requires a per-country theme from Strapi with a default fallback; the story does not mention it. The owner accepted delivering it in this change, with no runtime contrast check (rejection R-3, Q7).
The engineering reference requires all user-facing copy to come from Strapi except the fallback; the story only covers field copy, not navigation, progress and leave-dialog copy.
The story says errors appear when a field fails validation but not when they are shown; the gap checklist requires stating when validation messages appear.

The story has no loading state; the engineering reference requires explicit loading states and the design reference requires them to be announced. The owner added a visible loader and fallback loading copy (rejection R-2).
The story does not say what happens when Strapi is unavailable; principle P3 requires a controlled message instead of a broken screen.
The story does not cover misconfigured content; principle P3 and the architecture require validating content before use and showing a controlled message.
The story does not cover an empty form step; the engineering reference requires an explicit empty state.
The story does not cover repeated activation of continue; the gap checklist requires handling double submission.
The story only covers going back; the architecture states that wizard data survives reloading, and the owner kept the rule that unconfirmed values are not stored (rejection R-1).
The story does not say whether data is shared between countries or how long it lives; the architecture keeps a store per country in session storage, discarded when the tab closes.
The story does not cover entering a later step directly; the gap checklist requires stating direct entry, and a later step must not be reached without valid earlier data.
The story allows the business team to change fields at any time but does not say what happens to data stored under an earlier configuration.
The story does not say where entered personal data may travel; principles P4 and P5 and the engineering reference require it not to be sent to Strapi or logged in this step.
The story has no accessibility criteria; principle P6 and the design reference require programmatic labels, associations and an automated scan.
The story has no accessibility criteria; the design reference requires keyboard-only completion with visible focus, checked in every user interface review.
The story has no responsive criteria; the design reference sets the reference widths, reflow to 320 px and minimum target size.
The story has no motion criteria; the design reference requires respecting the reduced-motion preference.
The story does not say what happens to values not yet confirmed when the page is reloaded or closed; the owner required the browser's native leave confirmation (rejection R-1).

The story does not say what happens to values not yet confirmed when the person leaves the wizard; the owner required the application's own confirmation dialog when leaving to the root or another country (rejection R-1).
The owner stated that going back to the previous step does not ask for confirmation (rejection R-1); this criterion states that behavior and its effect on unconfirmed values.
